title: CharacterBody3D's rotation causes glitching for a RayCast3D
body: ### Tested versions -Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable (if 4.7.2 project opened) -Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description CharacterBody3D's rotation causes glitching in RayCast3D rotation. Same bug appears if a project was 'downgraded' from 4.7.2 to 4.7.1, it shows up even in a new scene. ### Description When a RayCast3D's `global_rotation_degrees` is assigned every physics frame, its debug shape (enabled via Debug → Visible Collision Shapes and `get_tree().debug_collisions_hint = true` in `_ready()` somewhere) flickers continuously and appears rendered twice at two different rotations, but in reality there is one ray on either of those two positions on every frame(according to tests with screenshots). The flicker persists even when the parent CharacterBody3D is not being rotated — i.e., when the body is completely stationary, the ray's debug shape still flickers as long as global_rotation_degrees is being assigned each frame. ### Quick Solution Replacing the assignment with the local property `rotation_degrees.x` makes the flicker disappear completely. ### ### script A ```swift extends CharacterBody3D const KEY_ROTATION_SPEED := 2.0 # radians per second var mouse_delta: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: var rotation_input := Input.get_axis("ui_right", "ui_left") if rotation_input != 0.0: rotate_y(rotation_input * KEY_ROTATION_SPEED * delta) ``` ### script B ```swift extends Node3D @onready var ray: RayCast3D = $RayCast3D func _ready() -> void: get_tree().debug_collisions_hint = true func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: ray.global_rotation_degrees.x = 120 ``` ### Scene Tree ``` Node3D (root) └── CharacterBody3D # script A ├── CollisionShape3D └── Node3D # script B └── RayCast3D ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Recreate the scene tree shown above. 2. Attach the scripts as indicated. 3. Enable Debug → Visible Collision Shapes 4. Run the scene (F5). 5. Click on the camera icon to rotate it to see the ray 6. Use arrows to rotate the CharacterBody3D ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [rotate-bug-472.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33032181/rotate-bug-472.zip)
